decisions.reason: It extends the firm's core wafer and process-integration know-how, so with strong in-house R&D and related customer needs management would usually keep and refine it rather than exit quickly.
Carrier wafers are very close to the firm's established substrate and thin-wafer handling business and fit its stated strategic direction, making continuation highly likely.

Although technically more demanding, the copper interposer glass wafer still builds on the firm's existing materials and packaging capabilities, and its R&D base gives it a good chance to learn and improve it commercially.
An off-the-shelf brand is close to the existing glass and quartz wafer offer and can leverage current production and customer relationships, even if the branding format itself may be adjusted.
Glass-based circuit boards are relatively distant from the firm's narrow core substrate business, so absorptive-capacity limits and resource focus make withdrawal the more likely choice.
